verdict.justification: A is the stronger meeting-ready recovery plan: it reconciles the source quantities to 9,555 sets including May, provides formula-driven scenario comparisons, and clearly explains the implications for all three products. Its four-week extended-shift window, “Tue 20-Feb to Mon 19-Mar,” avoids Louis Riel Day and delivers 20 production days, whereas B's February 5–March 2 window delivers only 19. A quantifies the resulting protection as 45 sets before the April deadline and 190 sets overall, giving management more actionable risk information than B's whole-day float discussion. B also reports incorrect Scenario 2 backlog completion dates—“Feb Sup done Feb 23” and “Nov–Feb POs finish Mar 20”—where the stated rates and calendar yield February 22 and March 19, as A reports. A's parameter-based scheduling is easier to revise when assumptions change, while B explicitly uses production inputs and hard-coded summary conclusions that require more manual coordination. Both deliverables address the requested scenarios and appropriately flag the assumed Grill Guard cycle time, but A offers the better-supported recommendation and more precise execution controls.
